name: CREtech New York 2026: event landing page for a real estate AI conference
title: CREtech New York 2026: event landing page for a real estate AI conference
answer: This is the landing page for CREtech New York 2026, a real estate AI conference on October 20 to 21, 2026 at the Javits Center in New York. Its most useful content is the attendee picture it promises: 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers and 20,000 or more pre-scheduled one to one meetings, with construction companies named among the groups converging. It is event marketing rather than research, and it contains no venture capital or investment data.

sections.body: It is a conference landing page published by CREtech for CREtech New York 2026, an event it calls the world's premier real estate AI conference. The page covers the event dates, October 20 to 21, 2026, the venue, the Javits Center in New York City, the audience it expects, the programme format and ticket sales. Its scope is promotional and logistical rather than analytical. The page states no publication date, and the text was harvested on 26 September 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents CREtech New York 2026 as the defining gathering for real estate in the age of AI, running October 20 to 21, 2026 at the Javits Center in New York. It says AI is transforming real estate and that the leaders shaping the industry are converging there, listing owners, developers, investors, occupiers, construction companies, brokers and technology leaders. Sessions are described as led by operators actively deploying AI across their portfolios rather than theory, with chief information officers, chief executives and managing directors sharing how they deploy technology, AI and new strategies. Speakers are said to come from global investors, developers and operators managing millions of square feet, which the page gives as the reason innovative startups attend. A meetings programme is said to facilitate more than 20,000 pre-scheduled one to one meetings with attendees from across the real estate ecosystem. The page also addresses sponsors and partners, offering brands a place alongside firms driving the industry forward, and promotes passes by role, warning that tickets are limited and prices will increase. It closes by saying the event is designed to turn insight into action and connections into deals.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source gives these figures: 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers and 20,000 or more pre-scheduled one to one meetings, on October 20 to 21, 2026 at the Javits Center in New York City. It claims the largest meetings programme in real estate and says speakers include operators managing millions of square feet. It gives no investment, funding or venture capital figures.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in construction can use this page to see where the adjacent real estate AI conversation is being staged and who the organiser claims will attend, since construction companies are named among the groups converging at the event. It signals that AI deployment by asset owners, developers and operators is the framing the real estate technology world is using, and that startups are expected to attend for that reason. It is useful as a pointer to an event and an audience, not as evidence about construction technology itself.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Construction

sections.body: The page is commercial event marketing and contains no research, data or analysis. It does not mention MetaProp, venture capital, funding rounds or tracking of venture flow across architecture, engineering and construction technology, so it does not support a claim about proptech capital reaching AEC. It covers only one event, gives no publication date, and its attendee and meeting figures are the organiser's own promotional claims.
